title_ar: ما الفرق بين قول المحدث في رواية بعض الصحابة عن بعض المغيبـات: موقوف له حكم الرفع، وقولهم : بل هذا من أخبار بني إسرائيل ؟
title_en: What Is the Difference between a Hadith Scholar Saying, of a Companion's Report about Matters of the Unseen, 'It Stops at a Companion but Has the Status of a Report Traced to the Prophet', and Their Saying, 'Rather This Is from the Reports of the Children of Israel'?
body_ar: الشيخ المفضال السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته أسأل الله العظيم أن يبارك فيكم ويتقبل منا ومنكم صالح القول والعمل. شيخنا ما الفرق بين قول المحدث في رواية بعض الصحابة عن بعض المغيبـات: موقوف له حكم الرفع، وقولهم : بل هذا من أخبار بني إسرائيل ؟ جزاكم الله كل الخير الجواب : ما حكمه الرفع إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه و سلم إذا صح إسناده إلى الصحابي وجب تصديقه و ما كان من الإسرائيليات فلا يصدق و لا يكذب
body_en:
Most excellent Sheikh, peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings. I ask God the Magnificent to bless you and to accept from us and from you good word and deed.

Our Sheikh, what is the difference between a hadith scholar saying, of a report by some of the Companions about matters of the unseen, that it is 'a report stopping at a Companion (mawqūf) which has the status of a report traced to the Prophet (marfūʿ)', and their saying, 'rather this is from the reports of the Children of Israel'? May God reward you with all good.

Answer: What has the status of being traced to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), if its chain of transmission to the Companion is sound, must be believed. And what belongs to the Israelite reports (isrāʾīliyyāt) is neither affirmed as true nor denied as false.

flags.context: و ما كان من الإسرائيليات فلا يصدق و لا يكذب
options: material transmitted from the earlier scriptural communities
flags.note: Technical term of Qur'anic exegesis and hadith criticism for narrative material of Jewish or Christian provenance transmitted by early Muslims. Kept transliterated with a plain gloss; not in the project glossary, and a candidate for addition alongside the items listed in section 13.

translator_notes: The distinction is a rule of what the believer owes each class of report, not a grading of authenticity: the first must be believed, the second is neither affirmed nor denied, which is the classical position drawn from the report 'do not believe the People of the Book and do not disbelieve them'. The Sheikh does not cite that report here and it has not been supplied.

المغيبات ('matters of the unseen') is the questioner's term and marks why the distinction matters: a Companion reporting something unknowable by ordinary means is presumed to have it from the Prophet, unless it is the sort of thing that came from the earlier scriptures.
